chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fadalah ibn Ayoub, from Bashir al-Hudhali, from Ajlan Abu Salih, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'When the newborn is born, we give him wine to drink.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever gives a newborn wine to drink, or said: an intoxicant, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will quench him with al-Hameem (scalding water), even if He has forgiven him.'

key_terms.الْحَمِيم: Scalding water (a specific drink in Hell)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of giving wine to a newborn child according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the specific act of giving wine to a newborn with the unique punishment of 'al-Hameem' (scalding water), as detailed in Surah Al-Imran. This highlights a distinct eschatological consequence for this specific act, separate from general forgiveness, emphasizing the gravity of introducing intoxicants to the innocent. The chain of transmission through prominent Kufan scholars underscores its reliability within the Shia tradition.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Bashir Al Huzalay, from Ajlan Abu Salih who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The child is born so (if) we quench it from the wine’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whoever quenches a newborn with wine’, or said: ‘intoxicant’, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would Quench him from the scalding water, even though He<sup>azwj</sup> may have Forgiven him’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah abu Ayyub from Bashir al- Hudhaliy from ‘Ajlan abu Salih who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if we can make a new born drink wine. He (the Imam) said, ‘If one makes a child drink wine’ or he said, ‘intoxicating liquor, Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, will make him drink al-Hamim (boiling water that roasts the face when drinking) of hell even if He forgives him.’”
